disclaimer: Informational stay-limit summaries for trip math. Not legal advice, not an admission decision, and not a substitute for the stamp in your passport or a visa sticker. Rules change. Each row has a source and a last-verified date.

rules.summary: Visa-free short stay of 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen Area.
rules.notes: Count every day of presence, including the entry day and the exit day, in all Schengen countries together. Bulgaria and Romania are members. Cyprus and Ireland are not. A short-stay calculator is published by the European Commission. Passport should be valid for at least three months after the intended departure.
rules.sourceTitle: European Commission short-stay calculator

rules.summary: Visa-free as a Standard Visitor, usually for up to 6 months on each visit.
rules.notes: There is no Schengen-style 90/180 cap for US visitors. Border officers decide the period of stay. Work is not allowed on a Standard Visitor permission.
rules.sourceTitle: GOV.UK Standard Visitor

rules.summary: US citizens do not need a visa or an eTA. A visit is usually authorized for up to 6 months.
rules.notes: The officer at the border sets the authorized stay. This row uses six months as the published usual maximum, not a guarantee.
rules.sourceTitle: IRCC eTA eligibility (US citizens are exempt)

rules.summary: Visa exemption for a temporary visitor stay of up to 90 days.
rules.notes: The exemption is for tourism, business meetings, and similar temporary visits. Paid work needs a different status. Confirm the current exemption table before travel.
rules.sourceTitle: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — visa exemption

rules.summary: Tourist visa exemption of up to 30 days, in force from 15 September 2026.
rules.notes: The 60-day exemption was revoked. Land and sea entries under the exemption are generally limited to twice per calendar year. Tourism only. Complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card. Passport validity of six months is commonly required.
rules.sourceTitle: Royal Thai Embassy — tourist visa exemption (effective 15 September 2026)

rules.summary: No visa for tourism. The maximum visitor stay is 180 days, as granted on entry.
rules.notes: Instituto Nacional de Migración can stamp fewer than 180 days. The stamp is the limit that matters. This row uses the published maximum.
rules.sourceTitle: Instituto Nacional de Migración

rules.summary: Visa on arrival for up to 90 days in a 180-day period, measured from first entry.
rules.notes: The stay may be continuous or split. It is not a work visa. Passport must be valid at least six months from arrival. BorderMath applies a rolling 90/180 count, which matches a single cluster of visits against that cap. The stamp controls.
rules.sourceTitle: UAE Embassy in Washington — visas for US citizens

rules.summary: Visa-free short stay of 90 days in any 180-day period. The UK is not in Schengen.
rules.notes: British citizens are third-country nationals for the short-stay rule. Days in every Schengen country share one pool.
rules.sourceTitle: European Commission short-stay calculator

rules.summary: Visa Waiver Program with ESTA. Up to 90 days per admission, not extendable.
rules.notes: ESTA is an authorization, not a visa, and does not guarantee entry. Time in Canada, Mexico, or nearby islands can count against the same 90-day admission if you return to the US.
rules.sourceTitle: US Department of State — Visa Waiver Program

rules.summary: eTA required for air travel. A visit is usually authorized for up to 6 months.
rules.notes: Apply for the eTA before flying. The border officer sets the actual authorized stay.
rules.sourceTitle: IRCC — Electronic Travel Authorization

rules.summary: Visa exemption for a temporary visitor stay of up to 90 days.
rules.notes: Temporary visitor status does not allow paid work.
rules.sourceTitle: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — visa exemption

rules.summary: Tourist visa exemption of up to 30 days from 15 September 2026.
rules.notes: The UK is on the 30-day tourist exemption list. Land and sea entries under the exemption are generally limited to twice a calendar year.
rules.sourceTitle: Royal Thai Embassy, London — visa information

rules.summary: British passports are visa-exempt for tourism, up to 180 days as granted on entry.
rules.notes: The INM admission stamp can be shorter than 180 days.
rules.sourceTitle: Instituto Nacional de Migración

rules.summary: Free visa on arrival, up to 90 days in a 180-day period from first entry.
rules.notes: FCDO describes the stay as continuous or split, provided the total does not exceed 90 days in that 180-day period. Passport must be valid for at least six months after arrival.
rules.sourceTitle: GOV.UK — UAE entry requirements

rules.summary: Visa-free short stay of 90 days in any 180-day period.
rules.notes: One shared pool for every Schengen country.
rules.sourceTitle: European Commission short-stay calculator

rules.summary: Visa-free as a Standard Visitor, usually for up to 6 months.
rules.notes: Canadian citizens do not need a visa for a standard visit.
rules.sourceTitle: GOV.UK Standard Visitor

rules.summary: Canadian citizens generally do not need a visa or ESTA. Visits are often admitted for up to 6 months.
rules.notes: This is not the Visa Waiver Program. Customs and Border Protection decides the period of admission.
rules.sourceTitle: US Department of State — citizens of Canada and Bermuda

rules.summary: Visa exemption for a temporary visitor stay of up to 90 days.
rules.notes: Temporary visitor status does not allow paid work.
rules.sourceTitle: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — visa exemption

rules.summary: Tourist visa exemption of up to 30 days from 15 September 2026.
rules.notes: Canada is on the 30-day tourist exemption list published with the September 2026 revision.
rules.sourceTitle: Royal Thai Embassy — tourist visa exemption

rules.summary: Canadian passports are visa-exempt for tourism, up to 180 days as granted on entry.
rules.notes: The INM stamp can be shorter than the maximum.
rules.sourceTitle: Instituto Nacional de Migración

rules.summary: Visa on arrival listed for a 90-day visit.
rules.notes: Carrier and airport tables list Canada for a free visa on arrival and a 90-day visit. Confirm the current ICP/GDRFA rule and the stamp. BorderMath counts 90 days in any 180.
rules.sourceTitle: Emirates — UAE visa information (90-day visit list)

rules.summary: Visa-free short stay of 90 days in any 180-day period.
rules.notes: One shared pool for every Schengen country.
rules.sourceTitle: European Commission short-stay calculator

rules.summary: Visa-free as a Standard Visitor, usually for up to 6 months.
rules.notes: Japanese citizens do not need a visa for a standard visit.
rules.sourceTitle: GOV.UK Standard Visitor

rules.summary: Visa Waiver Program with ESTA. Up to 90 days per admission.
rules.notes: ESTA required before travel. The admission cannot be extended inside the country.
rules.sourceTitle: US Department of State — Visa Waiver Program

rules.summary: eTA required for air travel. A visit is usually authorized for up to 6 months.
rules.notes: The border officer sets the authorized stay.
rules.sourceTitle: IRCC — Electronic Travel Authorization

rules.summary: Tourist visa exemption of up to 30 days from 15 September 2026.
rules.notes: Japan is on the 30-day tourist exemption list.
rules.sourceTitle: Royal Thai Embassy — tourist visa exemption

rules.summary: Japanese passports are visa-exempt for tourism, up to 180 days as granted on entry.
rules.notes: The INM stamp can be shorter than the maximum.
rules.sourceTitle: Instituto Nacional de Migración

rules.summary: Visa on arrival listed for a 90-day visit.
rules.notes: Carrier tables list Japan for a 90-day visit on arrival. Confirm with ICP/GDRFA. BorderMath counts 90 days in any 180.
rules.sourceTitle: Emirates — UAE visa information (90-day visit list)

rules.summary: A short-stay visa is required. If one is issued, the 90/180 ceiling still applies.
rules.notes: The sticker can authorize fewer than 90 days. This row alerts both that a visa is required and when a planned short stay would break 90/180.
rules.sourceTitle: European Commission — Schengen visa policy

rules.summary: A Standard Visitor visa is required. If granted, the permission is usually up to 6 months.
rules.notes: Apply before travel. The vignette and the decision letter set the actual permission.
rules.sourceTitle: GOV.UK Standard Visitor

rules.summary: A visitor visa is required. India is not in the Visa Waiver Program.
rules.notes: A B-1/B-2 admission, if issued, is often up to six months and is written on the I-94. This row uses six months only as that usual maximum.
rules.sourceTitle: US Department of State — visitor visas

rules.summary: A visitor visa is required. An eTA alone is not enough.
rules.notes: If a visa is issued, the authorized stay is decided at the border and is often up to six months.
rules.sourceTitle: IRCC — visit Canada

rules.summary: A visa is required before travel.
rules.notes: India is not on the visa-exemption list. The sticker sets the period of stay. BorderMath does not invent a day cap.
rules.sourceTitle: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — visas

rules.summary: Tourist visa exemption of up to 30 days from 15 September 2026.
rules.notes: India is on the revised 30-day tourist exemption list. Land and sea entries under the exemption are generally limited to twice a calendar year.
rules.sourceTitle: Royal Thai Embassy — tourist visa exemption

rules.summary: A visa is required unless a published exception applies.
rules.notes: A valid visa for the United States, or certain residence permits, can replace a Mexican visa. Check the current INM exception list. No day cap is assumed until an admission is granted.
rules.sourceTitle: Instituto Nacional de Migración

rules.summary: A visa arranged before travel is required for an ordinary Indian passport.
rules.notes: Holders of a valid US visa, US green card, or UK/EU residence permit may qualify for a short visa on arrival in Dubai (often 14 days). That exception is not applied automatically here. Passport validity of six months is commonly required.
rules.sourceTitle: UAE government portal — do you need a visa
